items.text: Roughly Rs 6-8 LPA gross for IBPS/SBI PO, basic pay around Rs 48,480 under the current bipartite settlement, in-hand around Rs 65,000-76,000 a month depending on posting.

items.heading: Every "Which Bank Is Better"
items.text: Every "which bank is better" comparison eventually comes down to six practical differences. None of them make one side objectively correct, they just suit different life stages and priorities.

items.heading: There Is No Single "Banking
items.text: There is no single "banking entrance exam." There are four real doors, and most serious candidates prepare for more than one at the same time to widen their odds.

visuals.heading: Public Sector Vs Private Bank: the Real

rows: Written exam first: IBPS or SBI Prelims + Mains + interview. No direct walk-in hiring for officer or clerk cadre.
Direct campus or off-campus hiring, or a structured PO program (HDFC Future Bankers, Axis Young Bankers, ICICI PO Program, IDFC FIRST Emerging Bankers). No common written exam.
Slower and seniority-linked: 5-7 years typical for the first officer promotion, with cadre-based exams (JAIIB, CAIIB) able to speed it up.
Faster and performance-linked: promotions in 2-3 years are common for people who hit targets consistently, but there is no guaranteed timeline.
High. Public sector bank roles carry pension/NPS benefits, near-permanent tenure after confirmation, and limited scope for performance-based termination.
Lower. Private banks can and do exit underperformers, especially in sales-heavy roles, and headcount moves with business cycles.
